title: Design: the Remove tab, its question and the result
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin whose role has 'Settings — Parts', 'See Financial Data', 'Customers — View' and 'Customers — Create & Edit'.
  • Have a new tier for this test, tier A, with a name no other tier uses.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, on tier A for work orders and tier A for Part Sales.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B, on tier A for work orders and Default for Part Sales.
  • Use a desktop browser window exactly 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom, so the screen matches the design pictures' size.
custom_steps:
1. Click the Tiers tab on Settings › Pricing.
  2. Click tier A's row on the Tiers list.
  3. Click the Customers tab.
  4. Click Manage Customers.
  5. Click the Remove Customers tab.
  6. Tick customer A.
  7. Click Remove 1 Customer.
  8. Click Remove in the question.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Tiers list shows tier A.

Step 2:

  • Tier A's page opens.

Step 3:

  • The Customers tab shows.

Step 4:

  • The dialog opens.

Step 5:

  • The Remove Customers tab is selected with its count; the last column reads "Take Off" tier A's name "for", and each row names its channels in gray, as in picture 9.16.

Step 6:

  • The dark bar reads 1 selected; the footer reads "Removing 1 customer: 1 for both." and the button is red, "Remove 1 Customer", as in picture 9.17.

Step 7:

  • A question titled "Remove 1 Customer?" reads "Removing 1 customer: 1 for both. They go back to Default for the channels you picked. Parts already on their work orders keep their prices."
  • Its buttons are Keep Customers and a red Remove, with an X at the top right, as in picture 9.18.

Step 8:

  • The tab lists customer B; a white message reads "1 customer taken off" tier A's name, with "They're back on Default for the channels you picked. Existing work orders and Part Sales keep their prices and tier."
  • The Customers tab count drops by one, as in pictures 9.19 and 9.20.
